assessment: The incumbent renders caption-video combinations and retains earlier previews, supporting inspection and historical access. Its weakness may be identifying intended inputs across repeated saves and completion order, rather than rendering itself: H1-O3 records reversed completion order and H1-O4 records unexpected inputs, but their causal connection is unproven. Only 20/30 sessions met the time target. H1-O7 limits a general rendering-bottleneck account: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in 5–11 minutes without uncertainty. H1-O6 leaves festival capacity unknown; sampled demand does not establish peak headroom.

openings.claim: An immutable requested video-caption pair, carried through rendering and displayed beside the download, could reduce unintended-version previews while preserving embedded output and historical access.
openings.delta: Identify previews by their requested source pair and edit revision, independently of completion numbering; retain each delivered pair and its original caption text.
openings.prediction: With deliberately reversed completion order, editors select their intended pair and artifact source hashes match that pair. Persistent mismatches despite correct selection would implicate worker input handling.
openings.probe: In private staging, replay demonstration edits involving two video cuts and multiple captions. Record intended pair before download and compare it with rendered source hashes; preserve access to the prior delivered pair. Timebox implementation and editor exercises within the stated allowances.
assumptions: Source snapshots can be bound atomically.
Implementation and retained snapshots fit the existing resource limits.

openings.claim: Do late sessions lose most time before the intended render becomes available, or after availability while identifying and inspecting it?
openings.delta: Discriminate scheduling/render latency from preview selection and interpretation before choosing a speed intervention.
openings.prediction: A predominantly pre-availability delay supports investigating redundant queued renders; a predominantly post-availability delay supports improving identification and inspection.
openings.probe: Combine timestamped render events with brief staging editor observations: mark final edit, intended-pair readiness, selection, and verified playback. Compare repeated-edit sequences against single corrections, using the same footage and the remaining editor-day allowance.
assumptions: Intended pairs can be independently established.
Demonstration tasks approximate relevant editing behavior; they cannot establish the 30-session success measure.
